flashcards.q: Default log buckets and their rules?
flashcards.a: _Required: Admin Activity/System Event audit logs + Access Transparency, fixed 400-day retention, free, cannot be modified or disabled. _Default: everything else, 30 days default, project-level retention configurable 1-3,650 days; shortening triggers a 7-day grace period (unqueryable but restorable).

Ingestion ~$0.50/GiB after first 50 GiB/project/month; retention $0.01/GiB/month beyond 30 days; vended network logs ~$0.25/GiB separate (~). Routing one entry to N destinations bills storage N times.

Exclusion filters on the _Default sink: health-check access logs often exceed half of total volume; GKE system info-level logs follow. Filtering before ingestion beats every downstream optimization because it stops the meter entirely.

SQL querying directly over log buckets via BigQuery dataset links without duplicating storage or paying routing costs - the compliance-analysis path that avoids double billing versus sinking copies into BigQuery separately.

flashcards.q: SLO alerting chain end to end?
flashcards.a: SLI (good/total ratio) -> SLO target -> error budget (complement) -> burn rate = consumption speed vs plan -> multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts: page when 1h burn >=14.4x AND 5m >=14.4x; ticket at 6h >=6x AND 30m >=6x (~).

Arithmetic: 14.4x sustained consumption exhausts a 28-day 99.9% error budget in about an hour. The constant derives from budget-exhaustion math (Google SRE workbook); the pairing with a confirmation window suppresses blips while catching real spikes.

Head-based decides at trace start - cheap but randomly drops interesting traces. Tail-based buffers spans and keeps slow/erroring traces while sampling healthy ones down - better signal for rare bugs, costs collector buffering. Critical paths use tail-based.

flashcards.q: What does billing export to BigQuery enable?
flashcards.a: Spend becomes SQL: top movers week-over-week, label/project attribution, commitment coverage analysis, automated alerts via Pub/Sub. Combined with deploy-time label enforcement (org policy), attribution becomes mechanical rather than archaeology.

flashcards.q: The GCP discount stack in priority order?
flashcards.a: Spot VMs for interruptible work (60-91% off) > committed use discounts on measured stable baselines (1yr/3yr) > automatic sustained-use discounts (~30% net full-month, eligible families). Rightsizing before discounts - committing to waste just discounts it.

Charges arriving no sooner than September 2027: ~$0.35/month per metric reference in a policy plus per-point query charges (~), with contract grandfathering windows. Prepare by auditing dead policies and consolidating conditions - not by deleting working alert coverage.

SLI measures the wrong plane: health endpoints pass while real flows fail; server-side latency excludes client-perceived time; long windows average away recurring bad periods. Fix with client-perspective synthetic transactions, per-endpoint SLIs, and segment slicing (region/tenant/version).

flashcards.q: What makes an error-budget policy real vs decoration?
flashcards.a: Pre-agreed consequences with executive sponsorship: >50% weekly burn triggers reliability review, >90% freezes feature deploys until recovered, pages link to budget impact. Without documented teeth agreed upfront, the SLO is a dashboard nobody acts on.
